# nish/synth

Short sounds made from nothing: square, triangle and noise voices with a pitch slide and a decaying envelope, mixed into an array of `f64` samples. Nothing is sampled or copied; a sound is arithmetic.

```ts
import {
  SYNTH_NOISE,
  SYNTH_SQUARE,
  SYNTH_TRIANGLE,
  synthSemitone,
  synthSilence,
  synthTone,
} from "nish/synth";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { SYNTH_SQUARE, SYNTH_TRIANGLE, synthSemitone, synthSilence, synthTone } from "nish/synth";

const RATE: i32 = 22050;
const out: f64[] = synthSilence(0.2, RATE);
synthTone(out, RATE, 0.0, 0.2, 440.0, 220.0, SYNTH_SQUARE, 0.25, 8.0);
synthTone(out, RATE, 0.05, 0.1, synthSemitone(440.0, 7), synthSemitone(440.0, 7), SYNTH_TRIANGLE, 0.2, 12.0);
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-callout type="info">

A sound starts as silence of its length and gains voices one at a time,
each added into the samples already there:

</scalar-callout>

The samples are not clipped: a voice stays inside `-volume..volume`, so
voices whose volumes sum to at most 1 stay inside `-1..1`, and what plays
them (a WAV writer, a page's audio buffer) clips the rest. The sample rate
is the caller's, passed to every function, so one program can make sounds
for a 22050 Hz file and a 48000 Hz page alike.

Pure: no capability, no I/O and no clock. The noise voice is a fixed
xorshift sequence, so the same call gives the same samples every time.

## Functions

### synthSemitone

The frequency `semitones` equal-tempered steps above `base`.

```ts
function synthSemitone(
  base: f64,
  semitones: i32,
): f64
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="f64" required>

the starting frequency in Hz

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="semitones" type="i32" required>

how many steps up; negative steps go down

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="f64">

`base × 2^(semitones / 12)`

</scalar-field>

### synthSilence

`seconds` of silence: an array of zero samples, one at least.

```ts
function synthSilence(
  seconds: f64,
  sampleRate: i32,
): f64[]
```

<scalar-field name="seconds" type="f64" required>

how long; zero, negative or NaN is one sample

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sampleRate" type="i32" required>

samples a second

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="f64[]">

`seconds × sampleRate` samples of 0.0, at least one

</scalar-field>

### synthTone

Add a voice into `out` from `start` seconds for `length` seconds. Its pitch
slides from `f0` to `f1` Hz on a log scale, and its loudness starts at
`volume` and falls by a factor of e every `1 / decay` seconds. A 2 ms attack
and a 5 ms release keep the ends from clicking. The voice stops at the end
of `out`; it never grows the array.

Nothing is added for a sample rate, start or length that is not positive
(a start of 0 is fine), for a frequency that is not positive, or for a
start or length too long to count in samples.

```ts
function synthTone(
  out: f64[],
  sampleRate: i32,
  start: f64,
  length: f64,
  f0: f64,
  f1: f64,
  wave: i32,
  volume: f64,
  decay: f64,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="out" type="f64[]" required>

the samples to add into

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sampleRate" type="i32" required>

samples a second that `out` is at

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="start" type="f64" required>

where the voice begins, in seconds from the first sample

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="f64" required>

how long the voice lasts, in seconds

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="f0" type="f64" required>

the starting pitch in Hz

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="f1" type="f64" required>

the ending pitch in Hz

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="wave" type="i32" required>

`SYNTH_SQUARE`, `SYNTH_TRIANGLE` or `SYNTH_NOISE`; any other value is noise

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="volume" type="f64" required>

the starting peak level; a negative level inverts the wave

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="decay" type="f64" required>

how fast the level falls, per second; 0 holds it

</scalar-field>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SYNTH_NOISE: i32`

Noise: a fresh random level each period of the pitch, so a falling pitch rumbles.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SYNTH_SQUARE: i32`

A square wave: +1 for the first half of each period, -1 for the second.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`SYNTH_TRIANGLE: i32`

A triangle wave: a straight rise from -1 to +1 and a straight fall back.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
